analysis.title: Investors' Outlook: Over the peak (November 2026)
key_insights: Vontobel expects economic growth, inflation and 10-year US Treasury yields to have peaked, and sees 2027 as flatter terrain with slower growth and possibly lower inflation.

October brought an AI-related tech sell-off. Chipmakers had their longest losing streak since 2008, while defensive sectors (staples, energy, health care) and quality and low-volatility styles outperformed.

The sell-off had four drivers: hotter US inflation pushing yields to two-decade highs, worries about financing AI buildout with debt, CXMT memory-chip progress raising pricing-power concerns (hitting South Korea and Taiwan), and crowded positioning in a few AI winners.
Vontobel says the AI cycle has not peaked. Demand is strong, computing power is in short supply, and investors are rewarding companies that fund capex from their own profits.

The Multi Asset Investment Committee closed its high-yield overweight to neutral (favoring BB) and upgraded government bonds to neutral from underweight, adding duration ahead of a softer 2027 growth and inflation backdrop.
Overweights in equities, emerging-market stocks and gold are unchanged. Cash, commodities and alternatives are neutral. The overall bond stance remains underweight.

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on October 28, with two members favoring a 25 bps hike. The Fed median shows 2027 rates flat while markets price close to two more hikes. Vontobel expects the market to move toward the Fed.

Almost all of this year's rise in 10-year Treasury yields reflects higher real yields and a higher expected policy path, not higher inflation compensation or term premium. Vontobel sees this as reversible.

At around 5% the 10-year yield offers an attractive asymmetry. A rise of about 75 bps over 12 months is absorbed before a USD investor loses money, while a 100 bps fall implies a return above 12% (illustration, not a forecast).

High-yield spreads have widened, with stress spreading from CCC to BB and B. Yields are around 8%. Investment-grade spreads are thin, and AI-related issuance (Microsoft's planned bond sale) is set to resume, so returns should come from carry and rates, not spread tightening.

Oil: Brent went above USD 100 after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Vontobel's base case for 2027 is gradual normalization, with firmer prices in 1H and softer prices in 2H as supply recovers and restocking runs its course.
The US SPR is near its lowest level since 1982 with no meaningful refill yet. This supports prices in 1H 2027.

EUR/USD has fallen from above 1.20 in January to about 1.12. The France-Germany 10-year spread is near euro-crisis highs, driven mainly by French budget and political risk. Vontobel calls it a French problem, not a euro crisis, and expects EUR/USD at 1.10-1.15 until a budget passes.
The dollar's strength is seen as a rates-driven bounce, not a new uptrend. The rate advantage should peak in 1H 2027 and narrow afterward.
Key 2027 risks: a geopolitical supply shock (inflationary), fiscal sustainability in the US, France or UK, central banks over-tightening (recession), and an AI-spending reversal (deflationary).
Housing is showing early strain. The 30-year mortgage rate passed 7.6% in late October and mortgage applications fell.
Central banks have tightened: the ECB deposit rate is 2.50% (+50 bps), the Fed hiked 25 bps in September, and the BoJ policy rate is 1.25%, a 31-year high.

trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads look tight relative to volatility, and growth is expected to slow. BB is the strongest of the high-yield ratings.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight gold as a portfolio diversifier
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural demand from official institutions and investors, a muted growth outlook and elevated geopolitical uncertainty support gold.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher bond yields and real interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold.

risk_factors: Geopolitics is the main upside risk to inflation and downside risk to growth, including a Middle East escalation into a regional war.
Fiscal sustainability in the US, France or the UK could trigger higher yields and volatility.
Central banks may over-tighten, and housing weakness could spill into consumption and employment.
An AI-related downturn from overinvestment, weak adoption or a competing region's breakthrough.
Sticky core services inflation could keep the Fed hawkish.
OPEC+ cohesion could break down, pushing oil lower than expected.
Doubt about the Fed's resolve could hit longer maturities.
A French rating downgrade or failed budget vote could push EUR/USD toward 1.10.
AI financing strain: bonds of heavily indebted AI computing providers slumped.

Chart 2 (Bonds) shows approximate one-year total returns on the 10-year US Treasury under parallel yield shifts, with a loss only above about a 75 bps rise.

vol_and_positioning: Volatility is poised to stay elevated, per Vontobel.

geopolitical: Iran-aligned Houthi forces claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian energy and civilian infrastructure, sending Brent above USD 100.
The Strait of Hormuz was temporarily closed in 2026.
Trump threatened to curb diesel exports and secured Europe's agreement to coordinate the release of part of its diesel reserves.
Trump suspended parts of a Russia sanctions package days before it was due to take effect.
Vontobel says Trump may turn more attention abroad after the US midterms on November 3, with risks of tariff headlines or Middle East escalation.
France's budget deficit and political pressure ahead of the 2027 presidential election are widening French bond spreads.
Democrats are expected to take control of Congress in the US midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price close to two more hikes in 2027, and December tightening is a market expectation. Inflation is sticky and oil is above USD 100.
tension_points.bear_case: Vontobel expects the market to move toward the Fed's flat 2027 median. Energy drove the inflation rise, wages are moderate, and cyclical core PCE is drifting lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sticky core services inflation that does not ease would keep the extra hikes priced in.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is strong and computing power is in short supply. Earnings forecasts are rising and positioning is less stretched.
tension_points.bear_case: Debt-funded AI buildout faces higher borrowing costs, CXMT progress threatens pricing power, and positioning is concentrated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cloud providers failing to fund more AI spending from their own cash flows would keep the debt concern alive.

tension_points.bull_case: Restocking, including an unfilled US SPR near its lowest since 1982, supports prices in 1H 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Supply recovers from the Middle East and non-Middle East producers keep output robust. OPEC+ may compete for market share, pushing prices lower in 2H.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broader Middle East war removing significant supply would invalidate the normalization view.
